name: readme-expiry-semantics
prompt: The README says sessions 'are lost when the process stops' but does not explain the expiry rule, and the rule in code is subtle: a session expires after 30 minutes of IDLE time (LastSeen refreshes on every successful GET), and expiry is enforced lazily on read. Two changes: (1) in main.go, expose the ttl via a constant const sessionTTL = 30 * time.Minute and use it in main instead of the literal; (2) add a README section '## Expiry' with exactly these three sentences: 'A session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.' 'Reading a session refreshes its idle timer.' 'Expired sessions are removed when they are read.' The verifier checks the constant is used and the section exists verbatim.

gold.README.md:
# demo

A small session service. Sessions live in memory and are lost when the process
stops.

## Run

```sh
go run .
```

- `POST /session?id=abc&user=ada` creates a session.
- `GET /session?id=abc` reads one and refreshes its last-seen time.
- `GET /healthz` reports how many sessions are held.

## Test

```sh
go test ./...
```

## Expiry

A session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity. Reading a session refreshes its idle timer. Expired sessions are removed when they are read.
